_meta.test_definition: A datable MARK-EVENT on a private holding moves derived NAV >=5% vs last official NAV. Does the fund's premium/discount converge toward derived NAV BEFORE the next official NAV print (frontrun) or only after?

ADX_control.note: tight stable ~12-14% discount to DAILY NAV; no event-driven gap-then-converge; weekly vol < 4%

DXYZ_keystone.pre_print_behavior: Price was ALREADY far ABOVE derived NAV before the event (peak +190% premium $71.24 on 5/11 vs derived ~$28-29). Market was NOT anchored on the stale official NAV and NOT converging UP toward derived NAV; it was in a SpaceX-IPO-anticipation speculative blow-off trading at a 2.4x premium to even the post-IPO derived NAV.
DXYZ_keystone.on_event: IPO date 6/12 the premium COLLAPSED from +57.6% (6/11) to +18.0% (6/12), i.e., price fell TOWARD derived NAV from far above, the OPPOSITE of the frontrun-the-up-mark thesis.
DXYZ_keystone.post_event: By 6/24 price $25.34 = +3.2% premium = BELOW the post-IPO derived NAV (~$27-29). A discount-to-derived-NAV has opened.
DXYZ_keystone.hit_or_miss: MISS as a directional convergence frontrun. The naive 'price converges UP toward the higher derived NAV before the print' is REFUTED for DXYZ. Price was overshooting on the upside pre-event and de-rated through/after the event. The realized edge sign is INVERTED vs the long-the-discount thesis.
DXYZ_keystone.tradability: DXYZ is hard-to-borrow / squeeze-prone (the documented DXYZ short lesson); shorting the +190% premium was the correct ex-post trade but uncapturable at scale due to borrow.

RVI.pre_print_behavior: RVI also ran to +206% premium (5/13) then de-rated; on 6/24 still +45% premium, vastly above derived NAV $25.84. Same overshoot pattern as DXYZ.
RVI.hit_or_miss: INDETERMINATE / MISS-LIKE: price is nowhere near converging to derived NAV; it sits 35% above it. Premium is dominated by venture-beta sentiment, not NAV-anchoring. The 5% surprise is also SOFT (unclosed rounds).
RVI.next_official_print: RVI's next official NAV (June quarter, ~Aug filing) is the cold out-of-sample; not yet printed.

edge_summary.edge_armA_DXYZ_RVI: NEGATIVE / INVERTED on the keystone (DXYZ) and INDETERMINATE on RVI. The frontrun-the-up-mark hypothesis is REFUTED for the only hard event (SpaceX IPO): price did not converge UP toward derived NAV ahead of the print; it overshot far above and then fell toward it. The exploitable dislocation that DID exist (a +190% premium vs a ~$28 derived NAV) is a SHORT-THE-PREMIUM trade, not the long-the-discount frontrun, and is borrow-constrained.
edge_summary.edge_control_ADX_USA: ZERO qualifying events BY CONSTRUCTION. 100% Level-1 -> daily NAV already embeds any top-holding earnings move the same evening; derived(T-1)==official(T-1) always; no 5% pre-print surprise can fire. ADX trades a stable ~12-14% discount with weekly vol <4%, no event gap. This is the intended Arm-B null.
edge_summary.edge_A_minus_edge_B: NOT ESTIMABLE with sign/significance. Arm A produced 1 VERIFIED material event (DXYZ-SpaceX) + 1 SOFT (RVI); Arm B produced 0 events. With Arm A's single hard event a MISS (inverted), and Arm B structurally null, A-B cannot be shown POSITIVE. The moat (aggregation cost) is REAL and CONFIRMED (Arm A has discrete unobservable marks; Arm B has none) but the TRADE direction the spec hypothesized does not hold.

section7_verdict: FAILED (as specified) / RE-FRAMED. The >65% up-convergence hit-rate is NOT met (keystone is a directional MISS, N too low for significance regardless). edge(A)-edge(B) is not positive. BUT the negative result is itself the finding: in retail-driven single-name pre-IPO CEFs the premium is set by venture-beta sentiment and overshoots derived NAV on BOTH sides of an event, so the price is NOT anchored on the stale official NAV (the core premise of the frontrun). The aggregation-cost MOAT is confirmed; the mean-reversion-to-derived-NAV TRADE is not. Microstructure lesson encoded.

N_power_caveats.statement: N=1 hard event. No significance claim is made or possible. The SpaceX IPO is a single, idiosyncratic, once-ever event. Direction of the realized dislocation (premium overshoot then de-rate) is reported as a microstructure observation, not a backtested edge. Forward out-of-sample: DXYZ and RVI next official NAV prints (Q2, ~Aug 2026) can be scored cold against the derived NAVs recorded here ($27-29 DXYZ, $25.84 RVI).
